parts.label: Part 4
parts.article:
For my investigation into the history and uses of plant products, I have focused on the cultivation and production of saffron, an expensive bright yellow spice made from crocus flowers. Unlike most other species of crocus, the saffron crocus doesn’t flower in February or March, but in October, when it produces fragrant lilac-coloured flowers, which are harvested at that time. During the harvest, the flower petals are discarded and only the stigmas, the three dark orange- or red-coloured reproductive parts of the flower, are commercially used.
One person must pick for almost 400 hours to produce just one kilo of saffron, and amazingly, to produce just 50 grams, it takes about 14,000 individual stigmas. No wonder the spice is so expensive! After this painstaking harvesting, and to preserve the intensive taste, smell, and colour of the product, the stigmas are subject to a process of drying, by which some 98% of their moisture content is removed. This makes it possible to keep saffron on the shelf to be used for many years.
The highly prized spice is famous for the flavour and aroma it imparts, which are often compared to that of honey. Saffron is also prized for its rich golden colour, which makes food look so tempting and indulgent. If you want to buy some of this fabled spice, you will find that saffron is either sold as whole stigmas or ground up as a powder. Today, saffron is used in both Eastern and Western cuisines to add both colour and flavour to an enormous range of recipes, though cooks would agree that it is most commonly added to recipes for the cooking of rice, because somehow it seems to complement such dishes perfectly. It is found to varying degrees in Italian, Spanish, Indian, and Iranian food. Although food preparation is its most common present-day use, medical research indicates that saffron may have important applications as a drug in the clinical treatment of a number of eye disorders.
Patients given saffron in their regular diet seem to show remarkable signs of recovery from serious conditions. And although scientists are still unsure of exactly why, recent experiments with laboratory rats have shown saffron to be effective in protecting the animals from damage caused when they are exposed to potentially harmful lights.
Now, I’d like to give a few examples of how saffron has been used since ancient times.
Some of the earliest evidence of saffron cultivation comes from archaeological excavations dating back 4,000 years on the island of Crete, where paintings and other artefacts have been found indicating that women wore beautiful saffron-coloured clothes. This is the earliest evidence of saffron being used as a dye. During the Roman Empire, saffron oil was produced, which, because of both its colour and aroma, was used to create cosmetics. But only the wealthiest citizens could afford these. Another use of saffron was to be found in the public baths. There, saffron was used as a perfume to keep the places smelling fresh and aromatic.
It is even said that the streets of Rome were strewn with saffron threads to greet Emperor Nero as an extravagant and sweet-smelling gesture when he made a triumphal entrance into the city. Other parts of the ancient world used saffron extensively. One of the most well-known examples was in Persia, which is modern-day Iran, where saffron was a vital part of the process of manufacturing carpets, being used as a traditional dye, along with other natural products like berries and minerals. analyses.content: 录音中明确提到，要生产 50 grams（50克）藏红花，需要大约 14,000 个柱头（stigmas）。
One person must pick for almost 400 hours to produce just one kilo of saffron, and amazingly, to produce just 50 grams, it takes about 14,000 individual stigmas.
你可能听到了 "400" 或 "one"，但 400 是小时数，one 是 1 公斤，只有 14,000 对应题目问的 50 克。

After this painstaking harvesting, and to preserve the intensive taste, smell, and colour of the product, the stigmas are subject to a process of drying, by which some 98% of their moisture content is removed.
千万别填 "moisture"（水分），那是被移除的东西，而不是保存的方法。
题目问保存的方法，录音中说为了保存产品，柱头必须经过一个 drying（干燥）的过程。
If you want to buy some of this fabled spice, you will find that saffron is either sold as whole stigmas or ground up as a powder.
你可能听到了 "ground"（磨碎的），但那是形容词，题目空格前有不定冠词 "a"，所以需要填名词 "powder"。
题目问出售的形式，录音说要么是完整的柱头，要么是磨成 powder（粉末）。

Today, saffron is used in both Eastern and Western cuisines to add both colour and flavour to an enormous range of recipes, though cooks would agree that it is most commonly added to recipes for the cooking of rice, because somehow it seems to complement such dishes perfectly.
不要听到 Italian, Spanish 或 Indian 就填上去，这些是国家风味，不是具体的“菜肴（dishes）”种类。
录音提到厨师们最常把藏红花加到烹饪 rice（米饭）的食谱中。
Although food preparation is its most common present-day use, medical research indicates that saffron may have important applications as a drug in the clinical treatment of a number of eye disorders.
题目中的 "problems" 对应录音中的 "disorders"，所以你只需要填身体部位 "eye"。
录音中说医学研究表明藏红花可以作为药物治疗多种 eye（眼睛）的疾病。
录音提到实验显示藏红花能保护老鼠免受有害 lights（光线）的伤害。

And although scientists are still unsure of exactly why, recent experiments with laboratory rats have shown saffron to be effective in protecting the animals from damage caused when they are exposed to potentially harmful lights.
注意题目是问 "exposure to..."（暴露在...下），所以要抓取暴露的对象，而不是听到 animals 就填上去。

Some of the earliest evidence of saffron cultivation comes from archaeological excavations dating back 4,000 years on the island of Crete, where paintings and other artefacts have been found indicating that women wore beautiful saffron-coloured clothes.
你可能听到 "paintings"（画作），但这只是证据的来源，染料是用来染衣服的。
录音提到在克里特岛的画作显示女性穿着藏红花染色的 clothes（衣服）。
During the Roman Empire, saffron oil was produced, which, because of both its colour and aroma, was used to create cosmetics.
题目已经有了 "used for the production of..."，所以不能填 "oil"，因为油是原料，化妆品才是产出的成品。
录音说在罗马帝国，藏红花油被用来制造 cosmetics（化妆品）。
Another use of saffron was to be found in the public baths. There, saffron was used as a perfume to keep the places smelling fresh and aromatic.
不要填 "fresh" 或 "aromatic"，这些是形容词描述效果的，题目空格处需要一个名词。
录音说在公共浴场，藏红花被当作 perfume（香水/香料）使用，以保持空气清新。

One of the most well-known examples was in Persia, which is modern-day Iran, where saffron was a vital part of the process of manufacturing carpets, being used as a traditional dye, along with other natural products like berries and minerals.
你可能听到 "berries" 或 "minerals"，但这些是和藏红花并列的其他原料，不是最终制造的产品。
录音最后提到在波斯，藏红花是制造 carpets（地毯）的重要染料。
